instructions: Peel the eggplant and cut it into 8 rounds, each 1/2 inch thick. Sprinkle both sides with 2 tsp of the salt and set the rounds in a colander for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, dice 1/4 cup of onion and dice the tomatoes. Heat the olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat, add the onion and cook for 4 minutes, until soft.

Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, until they break down. Stir in the basil, the remaining 1 tsp salt and the pepper. Turn the heat to low and let it simmer while you cook the eggplant. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Rinse the salt off the eggplant and pat the rounds very dry with a towel.
Whisk the eggs in one shallow dish. Grate the Parmesan, stir it into the breadcrumbs in a second dish.
Dip each round in the egg, then press it into the crumbs on both sides.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large high-sided skillet over medium heat until a crumb sizzles right away. Fry 3 or 4 rounds at a time for 3 to 4 minutes on the first side, until golden. Flip them and cook the other side for 3 to 4 minutes. Transfer them to a paper towel lined plate.
Heat the broiler to high. Split the rolls and set them open on a baking sheet.
Spread a spoonful of the cooked tomatoes on each roll, set 2 eggplant rounds on the bottom half, then add more of the tomatoes and 1/4 cup of the mozzarella.
Broil for 2 to 3 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the bread is crisp. Watch closely.
Close the sandwiches and serve hot.
method_notes: No version has 20 ratings, so this is a fallback lead. Stetted (5.0 from 1) is the one that fits a lunch: eggplant salted for 15 minutes, breaded in egg and Parmesan crumbs, shallow fried and broiled on rolls with a quick fresh tomato sauce. Girl Heart Food salts for an hour and uses butter-toasted ciabatta, and the Methodist version bakes the slices. Parmesan is traditionally made with animal rennet, so choose a vegetarian Parmesan-style cheese if that matters.
